refnamediv.refpurpose: Replace regular expression with multibyte support

refentry.refsect1:
&reftitle.parameters;
pattern
The regular expression pattern.
Multibyte characters may be used in pattern.
replacement
The replacement text.
The following references are replaced:
\0 is the whole match, and \1 to \9 are the numbered capturing groups. Only one digit is read, so \10 is group 1 followed by the character 0. The $1 and ${1} forms are not supported and are left as written.
\k<name> and \k'name' are the named capturing groups, and \k<1> is a numbered one.
A group that did not take part in the match is replaced by an empty string. A reference to a group that does not exist is left as written.
If pattern contains a named group, numbered references such as \1 and \k<1> are not replaced and are left as written; \0 and \k<name> still work.
A backslash followed by any other character, or at the end of the string, is copied unchanged. \\ is not an escape sequence: \\1 gives a backslash followed by the content of group 1, so a literal \1 cannot be written.
string
The string being checked.
options
The search option. See mb_regex_set_options for explanation.
